# Best travel charger with multiple USB-C ports

**Top pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port.** Three reviewers pick it for travel: [TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026), [TechWise's GaN roundup](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026), and [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger) (best 100W).
- It has 3 USB-C ports plus 1 USB-A, and a foldable US plug.
- One USB-C port can deliver the full 100W alone. With two devices it splits about 65W/30W. With all four in use it splits about 45W/30W/10.5W.
- The downsides are weight (8.3 oz), no cable included, and a plug adapter needed abroad.
- Buy: the reviews link to Amazon through their "Check price" buttons, but I don't have a direct product URL. You can use [TechWise's review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) to get there.

**Other good options**

- **Anker Prime 67W (3-port), for a smaller bag.**
  - It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A, weighs 4.78 oz, and delivers 67W from either USB-C port alone.
  - With two ports in use it drops to about 65W, and with all three to about 64.5W.
  - It's the top pick in [VoyageHacks' comparison](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/).
  - It's a poor fit if you need a laptop and a tablet charging fast together.
- **Anker 737 (120W), for a power-hungry laptop.** It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A. See [TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026).
- **Epicka TA-105 Max (75W), if you want one device for charging and plug adapters.**
  - It has 3 USB-C ports, 2 USB-A ports, and swappable plugs that work in 200+ countries.
  - See [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel).
  - Every other charger here needs a separate adapter outside the US.
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2 USB-C + USB-A), the budget option.**
  - You can [buy it here](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) for $49.99 (list $59.99). That is a 2-pack, and the link goes to Baseus's US store.
  - With multiple devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W.
  - The page is an affiliate link.

**Tips**
- Pick by your heaviest device. A laptop needs about 65W or more.
- Plug the laptop into the highest-power USB-C port first. Charger wattage is shared across ports.
- For 100W, use a 5A e-marked USB-C cable. Standard cables are only rated for 60W.
- These chargers handle 100-240V, so abroad you only need a plug-shape adapter, not a voltage converter.

The sources disagree on the UGREEN's port count. VoyageHacks says four USB-C, while the other three say three USB-C plus one USB-A. I'd trust the majority, but check the listing before buying.
